artists.biography:
Reef are an English band from Glastonbury, England. The band members include Gary Stringer on vocals, Kenwyn House on guitar, Jack Bessant on bass and Dominic Greensmith on drums.

Although most members of Reef have West Country connections, it was not until the four members met in London that the band was formed.

In 1993 while Bessant and Stringer were looking for band members, House had met up with Dominic Greensmith (from Barnstaple, Devon) in London, and discussed forming a band. The foursome finally got together, and started to jam, producing the extremely rare "Purple Tape" demo.

After recording a couple of tracks, the band spent much of 1994 touring and building up a fan base. They signed to S2, an offshoot of Sony. Their first single "Good Feeling" was released on an independent label, but financed by Sony, then as an official Sony S2 release in early 1995. This paved the way for "Naked" which was used in a TV advert for the Sony MiniDisc in which a record company executive hears the track on MiniDisc, throws it out of the window disapprovingly, but a young man outside picks it up, listens to it and likes it (demonstrating the format's durability). There has been some disapproval of the band's participation in this campaign, but in interviews they have emphasised that they were a young band and were offered a chance that any young band would not resist.

perplexity.description:
Glow is a rock album by Reef released in January 1997 through Sony Soho Square. Produced by the band alongside acclaimed producer George Drakoulias, the album was recorded across multiple prestigious studios including Abbey Road, Real World Studios, and Sound City Studios in Los Angeles. The record marked a significant artistic leap for the band, demonstrating their evolution from their promising debut into a fully realized creative force.

The album entered the UK charts at number one and spawned several successful singles, most notably "Place Your Hands," which reached number six on the UK charts and became a cultural touchstone of the era. The track's popularity was amplified by heavy rotation on BBC Radio 1 and appearances on the television program TFI Friday, where the band became recurring performers. Glow captured the energy and optimism of youthful rock music, with its songs written organically during rehearsals, soundchecks, and tours rather than through formal songwriting sessions. The album's commercial success and critical acclaim established Reef as major players in the 1990s rock landscape, proving they had transcended their initial promise to become a genuinely significant band of their generation.
